messages.subject: Latex cyrillic
messages.subject_clean: Latex cyrillic
messages.body_plain:
My app generates reports which contain Cyrillic symbols by knit2pdf.
It works great on my local computer, but fails at shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> with such message:
Running 'texi2dvi' on 'report_ru.tex' failed.
LaTeX errors:
! Package fontenc Error: Encoding file `t2aenc.def' not found.
(fontenc)                You might have misspelt the name of the encoding.

I use such code to produce Cyrillic symbols:
\usepackage[T2A]{fontenc}
\usepackage[utf8]{inputenc}
\usepackage[english,russian]{babel}

How to enable Cyrillic symbols at shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>?
Maybe with xelatex but which fonts shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> has?

Thanks!

messages.subject: deployApp() won't bundle files outside of current directory for relative paths?
messages.subject_clean: deployApp() won't bundle files outside of current directory for relative paths?
messages.body_plain:
We have a directory structure that looks like:

```
MyApp1/
  server.R
  ui.R
MyApp2/
  server.R
  ui.R
Shared/
  library-functions.R
```

We `deployApp` from the app directory e.g. MyApp2, which has references like:

```
source('../Shared/library-functions.R')
```

runApp() works great, deployApp() deploys successfully, but the app fails on shinyapps with "cannot open file '../Shared/library-functions.R': No such file or directory"

Is the Shared folder not getting bundled with the app? Why doesn't deployApp() complain if this isn't allowed?

We worked around the issue using symlinks.

Could you try adding library(gpclib) to your code? I suspect the issue is that gpclib is a suggested package, which means it is not automatically-installed. By adding the library() call, shiny apps will detect it as a required package and install it.

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Data security
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Data security
messages.body_plain:
Selva, Charles,
Thank you for your questions and concerns.  Shinyapps.io was built to allow for the isolation of different people's application and data from each other.  As part of our paid tiers, you will be able to restrict access to who can see/use your application through the authentication mechanism we provide.  In the coming two weeks we will be introducing a new way to do authentication which would allow you to require people to authenticate through their Google Authentication, GitHub authentication or using password based authentication in our service.   None of these address the question of how you are storing your data within the application and how you go about reading/writing your data which would need to be managed by you in your application.  All access to the service is over SSL which is a best practice for eliminating a class of security exploits.

To answer Charles's request.  The entire infrastructure is hosted in a SAS70 compliant facility, any credit card information we gather will be managed by a 3rd party provider who is PCI compliant as we will not be storing any financial instruments in our system to avoid needing to meet the PCI requirements.  A few of the security standards you refer to Charles are only relevant for financial data hosting which we aren't really targeting for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>  In the interest of full transparency we have also put together some docs  <http://www.rstudio.com/about/eula/>which capture our various policies and how we would use data that we could collect.

This service is new and we know that there are certain use cases that may not be a good fit for a hosted offering.  if your organization doesn't typically allow data to leave their firewalls, then shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is unlikely to be the right fit for you and it might be better for you to consider an on-premise version of Shiny Server to host your applications on.

I hope this helps clarify the issue.  Feel free to send along any other questions you have.

-Tareef

Everyone will need to upgrade this shinyapps using the following command:

devtools::install_github("rstudio/shinyapps")
Thanks
-Andy

messages.subject: issue when wanting to use older version on Shiny(10.1) instead of newer (10.2)
messages.subject_clean: issue when wanting to use older version on Shiny(10.1) instead of newer (10.2)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I have built an application using Shiny 10.1 - not the latest version. When I run the app locally, it runs smoothly without any issue, but when I use deployApp() to put it on shinyapps, the application fails to load. There is no error in the whole process of deploying it to shinyapps, but the screen on deployed app on shinyapps quickly times out showing only the header. This behavior is similar to when I tried using Shiny 10.2(latest) locally.

Here is the link: https://sarang.shinyapps.io/vanmap/

So, one or more of the following could have happened:
1. The code is not right and that's why it breaks in shinyapps. -- doesn't look likely because faulty code would break in local runs too.
2. The application times out owing to connection to an external data source.-- How to prevent timeout when the program is connecting to data sources on the net?
3. Shinyapps has installed latest package of Shiny, instead of older version used locally -- What can I do to make shinyapps use a specific version of a package rather than the latest?

I checked logs, but could not find anything there. Maybe there is another possibility I am not considering.

Your help is highly appreciated. Thank you in advance.

Cheers,
-SB

Hope this helps,
Fereshteh

On Tuesday, December 9, 2014 3:16:04 AM UTC-5, Sarang Brahme wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I have built an application using Shiny 10.1 - not the latest version. When I run the app locally, it runs smoothly without any issue, but when I use deployApp() to put it on shinyapps, the application fails to load. There is no error in the whole process of deploying it to shinyapps, but the screen on deployed app on shinyapps quickly times out showing only the header. This behavior is similar to when I tried using Shiny 10.2(latest) locally.
>
> Here is the link: https://sarang.shinyapps.io/vanmap/
>
> So, one or more of the following could have happened:
> 1. The code is not right and that's why it breaks in shinyapps. -- doesn't look likely because faulty code would break in local runs too.
> 2. The application times out owing to connection to an external data source.-- How to prevent timeout when the program is connecting to data sources on the net?
> 3. Shinyapps has installed latest package of Shiny, instead of older version used locally -- What can I do to make shinyapps use a specific version of a package rather than the latest?
>
> I checked logs, but could not find anything there. Maybe there is another possibility I am not considering.
>
> Your help is highly appreciated. Thank you in advance.
>
> Cheers,
> -SB

messages.subject: App turns grey after few seconds
messages.subject_clean: App turns grey after few seconds
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I'm running an app locally and it works just fine. When I deploy it, however, it freezes and the page turns grey.

What the app does:
I have a .csv file with 519kb that contains my data that is stored in the app directory under a "data" sub-directory. The app then subsets my data according to a selected variable on the left panel and returns the first 2 rows and first 3 columns. It can be seen here https://balboni.shinyapps.io/bmf-teste/

to read the data, server.R executes:
dados = read.table("data/base.csv",header=T,sep=";",dec=",")
Is this an issue because of a local defined path to the file or is it how I should do it?

I followed the 5th lesson on http://shiny.rstudio.com/tutorial/lesson5/ but I don't know if/what I should change in my code regarding my data.

I have also tried to set a larger app size to check if the problem was with memory size:
shinyapps::configureApp("bmf-teste", size="xxlarge")
As I suspected, memory does not appear to be the problem.

Any ideas of why the problem persists and how to fix it?

Thanks

Bernardo

Thanks, Andy!

Changing the enconding to UTF-8 did the trick and now the app runs perfectly! Thank you very much for your help!

For future references, if anyone finds the same problem, can save ui.R and server.R with UTF-8 encoding in R Studio -> File -> Save with Encoding.

For the data file (in this case a .csv), open it with notepad and File -> Save As and then change the encoding in the bottom of the window to UTF-8. That should do it.

messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy,

Finally, it worked!

The logs on website did not show the error and I have no Javascript knowledge, so i went to 'Inspect Element' on the app page and found out that the 'leaflet-heatmap.js' had an issue with SSL (it was calling 'http://' instead of 'https://' and so Google Chrome chose to not run the Javascript. To overcome the issue, I changed two things:
1. Downloaded the JS file from internet to a separate 'www' folder within the folder where my ui.R and server.R resided. I used direct reference to JS file in my R code instead of the web reference.
2. The map file was also using non-SSL reference for the map TileLayer. I was using Stamen TonerLite. I googled the SSL version of the same link and pasted it in my code.

This has solved the issues for both, the map PNG file and heatmap JS file.
I hope this helps other people doing similar kind of stuff on Shinyapps. If there is a better way, I would be interested to know.

Cheers!
-Sarang

messages.body_plain:
I'm facing an issue when trying to include in my shiny app a markdown file which contains MathJax expressions.

in my UI.R I'm using `includeMarkdown()` to import the markdown file

```
includeMarkdown("test.md")
```

In the markdown file, I've added the following snippet to import the MathJax.js library.

```
<script type="text/javascript"
  src="http://cdn.mathjax.org/mathjax/latest/MathJax.js?config=TeX-AMS-MML_HTMLorMML">
</script>
```

In my machine, MathJax is correctly interpreted and displayed, but in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>, the MathJax formulas are not interpreted, i.e., I see the MathJax expressions in the text like this:

```
\(S=w_{1}, w_{2},\ldots,w_{k}\)
```

I also tried to add the MathJax.js to the `www/`folder of my app, and import it from there directly, just in case that shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is not allowing external connections from their servers, are you actually doing this? Anyway, this neither worked.

Is this a known issue? Is there something I'm missing? Thanks in advance

messages.subject: App works differently on shinyapps vis my desktop
messages.subject_clean: App works differently on shinyapps vis my desktop
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
 I am having an issue with this app again:

 https://johnpaul.shinyapps.io/VegShiny/

however, this time it is easy to repeat and I have an  a work around that might be useful for testing. The app works as expected on my desktop, the problems are only on shinyapps.

Before I had an error where if you chose "Soil Map" from the "Map Layers" box in the lower left, the app would often crash. Thanks to something done on the Rstudio end (My code had not changed) that no longer happens ever. However, there is now a new and related issue.

Problem:
 When you chose a "Map Layer' a "Layer Legend" modal appears (it is a conditional panel) and it should display a legend. However what happens now is that the modal appears, but the legend does not. If I examine the elements in the modal using my browser I find that they are of class "shiny-html-output shiny-bound-output recalculating", whatever that means. Note, on rare occasion, the legend will appear.

Work around:

At the bottom of the map, there is a long thin modal that allows you to show or hide various parts of the interface. If you uncheck the "Layer Legend" box, then chose a map layer and let it display, and then check the "Layer Legend" box the legend will display correctly. I think what this is doing is making it so that the outputs for the map and the outputs for the Legend are not longer updating at the same time. Why that matters I have no  clue.

Thanks for your help and I have pasted my showLogs() output below:

John Paul

These are all possibilities. The processing of the file happens in the external packages (tm package) and not by Shiny.
I suggest that you create a very simple text file, and use that as the source for your code change. If that works (I am pretty sure it would), then you know that it is the source file that causes problem. And then you need to narrow down what in the file is causing the problem. If you want you can send your file to us. We can't promise to spend too much time on this, but it might something that we can figure out with a few minutes of time.

messages.subject: iframe error - embedding local html file
messages.subject_clean: iframe error - embedding local html file
messages.body_plain:
I 'm working on a Shiny app that will (hopefully) write an HTML file and then embed that file via iframe.  The entire app's code is here: https://github.com/joebrew/ShinyApps/tree/master/sliv2.

The app runs perfectly on my local machine (feel free to test yourself by forking <https://github.com/joebrew/ShinyApps/fork> it), but fails when deployed to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>.  I suspect that this has to do with http vs. https protocol, and how to actually point the iframe locally (as opposed to an external URL).

The app <https://joebrew.shinyapps.io/sliv2/> deployed on shinyapss.io <http://shinyapss.io> yields these errors:

Failed to load resource: net::ERR_NAME_RESOLUTION_FAILED
Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 405 (Method Not Allowed)

The specific lines in question in the server.R file are 140-150:
# Define path to html file
addResourcePath("library", paste0(root, "/www/index"))

# Render html leaflet map into iframe
output$help <- renderUI({
  tags$iframe(
    seamless="seamless",
    #src = "https://localhost://www/index/index.html", # doesn't work
    src="library/index.html",
    height = "600",
    width = "100%")
})

Any help is greatly appreciated.

>

Hi Tommy,

Please post the sessionInfo() of your local R environment. My guess is
that you were using Windows, and have called utils::setInternet2(TRUE)
somewhere, otherwise the error is entirely expected (HTTPS is not
directly supported).

When reading https resources, you are recommended to use more portable
solutions, such as RCurl (or httr), or downloader, to download the
files first: http://cran.rstudio.com/web/packages/downloader/index.html
(Note setInternet2() is a Windows-only solution)

Yihui

messages.subject: RODBC connection to an Microsoft Access Database fails when deployed
messages.subject_clean: RODBC connection to an Microsoft Access Database fails when deployed
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I may Shiny app pulls data from an MS Access database to make some graphs. The connection is made with RODBC :

odbcConnect("DSN_name")

This works well locally, but the app fails to make the database connection when deployed. I get the following error message:

Warning in odbcDriverConnect("DSN=WQSYNTH") :
[RODBC] ERROR: state IM002, code 0, message [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Data source name not found, and no default driver specified

My access database is only 12mb.

Does anyone know why this is happening. The Data source name is found when run locally, so why not when deployed?

Thanks for your time.

Cheers,
YD.

Thanks Yihui Xie and everyone, I have resolved the problem.

Instead of using fread the Google sheet directly from the URL, which only work with Windows:

fileURL <- "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1HqkFzMxhXwE2usiyhF-Qorje-uNWUdB7l3oz4TFzuSo/export?format=csv"
DF <- fread(fileURL, header=TRUE)

downloader:download the Google sheet as CSV into local drive then fread it (work with Windows and Ubuntu):

library(downloader)
fileURL <- "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1HqkFzMxhXwE2usiyhF-Qorje-uNWUdB7l3oz4TFzuSo/export?format=csv"
#DF <- fread(fileURL, header=TRUE)
localCSV <- "./gs.csv"
download(fileURL, localCSV, mode = "wb")
DF <- fread(localCSV, header=TRUE)
View(DF)

The next question will be how to tell the server not to overwrite the download Google sheet if no change has made.

           "Quintiles" = QUINTILES,
            "Others" =OTHERS)
  })
  output$dataset <- renderPlot({
    barplot(data=dataset)
  })
